name: Jacoby Meadows (Phase I)
headline: The Windsor and Loveland housing authorities built Jacoby Meadows Phase I, a 62-unit (61 income-restricted plus one employee unit), three-story senior (55+) building in west Windsor's Windshire Park neighborhood for households at 30% to 80% AMI, with a $1,450,000-a-year 2023 Round One 9% credit award from CHFA; it was completed and ribbon-cut in October 2025.
why_it_matters: It is Windsor's first new affordable senior rental, built on housing-authority-owned land with about $1.1M of town fee waivers and an HB22-1304 grant match, and it finished in 13 months after taking three CHFA rounds and a redesign to win credits.

status.label: Complete: ribbon cutting in the week of 2025-10-27
status.detail: Groundbreaking was held on 2024-08-14, the building topped out by 2025-03-25, and Mile High CRE reported on 2025-10-27 that Pinkard had completed Phase I and held a ribbon cutting earlier that week. Lease-up status and the CHFA placed-in-service date are not public. Phase II (61 units) was still seeking funding.

next_step: Watch for CHFA's placed-in-service record and any Phase II funding application (CHFA or Division of Housing).

background.text: The project took five years, three rounds of CHFA tax credit applications, a minor redesign and a significant redesign; the 2023 application followed the Town of Windsor raising the height limit from two stories to 40 feet, which allowed one three-story elevator building and prompted the new name.

The Windsor Town Board made senior housing a priority and the mayor asked WHA to target 55+ housing; the application notes Windsor had no senior tax credit property and the 48-unit Governor's Farm senior property had converted to market rate.

Local approvals in the application: preliminary plat and site plan submitted in late July 2022, final site plan expected March 2023 and final plat before the Planning Commission in April 2023; a community presentation on 2022-11-17 drew unanimous support.

Phase I carries site work and common space for a planned 123-unit senior campus: Phase II (61 units, connected by a covered walkway) and Phase III bungalows; Pinkard's president said Phase II was targeted three to five years after Phase I.
Construction met a bedrock-like layer and groundwater during sewer tie-ins, but framing finished in under two months and the 13-month build came in on time and on budget, per Pinkard.
Market study in the application: a 9.6% capture rate, against a 1BR market rent of $1,950.

discrepancies.text: CHFA lists the address as 15th Street at Windshire Drive, while the application gives 1500 Windshire Drive.

CHFA's award report names Loveland Housing Authority as owner, while its award description names Windsor Housing Authority and Loveland Housing Authority as developer and the trade press describes the project as built for Windsor Housing Authority.
The cost was given as $17.5 million at the August 2024 groundbreaking and $18 million at completion.

CHFA's award description lists 61 restricted units (49 one-bedroom, 12 two-bedroom) plus one employee unit, for 62 in all; its bedroom count covers only the 61 restricted units, so the employee unit's size is not stated.
